content: Metabolic surgery, often referred to as bariatric or weight-loss surgery, is a highly effective intervention for the management of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Procedures such as Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) and sleeve gastrectomy (VSG) are commonly performed to reduce food intake by creating smaller stomach pouches and bypassing portions of the digestive tract. These surgical techniques have demonstrated significant long-term benefits, including reductions in blood glucose levels, hemoglobin A1C, and cardiovascular risks. Importantly, these benefits are observed regardless of the patient’s body mass index (BMI), making these procedures applicable to a broad spectrum of individuals.
